title: Latency-mode kernel selector and prefill budget experiment
creator: Arielle Park
description:
Goal: Reduce p99 generation latency regressions introduced by FlashAttention v3 on long-context and mixed-batch workloads while preserving throughput and cost targets. We will implement a runtime modality called 'latency-mode' that biases the kernel selector toward lower-latency kernels when the request is flagged latency-sensitive (SLO-bound). The experiment couples the selector with a per-request prefill budget calculator to avoid repeated kernel handoffs during decode.

Background: Recent v3 rollouts reduced median cost but caused sporadic p99 spikes on decoder-heavy traces due to kernel handoffs during prefill->decode transitions. Existing kernel scoring favors throughput and memory efficiency; we need a complementary path that accepts some throughput loss for much steadier tail latency when the app requests low-latency operation.

Approach / Plan:
- Implement a request-scoped flag (latency_mode=true) propagated from API layer for routes that require strict latency.
- Add a kernel selector policy that exposes a tunable latency_weight and prefill_handoff_threshold. The selector will score candidate kernels using latency_weight * estimated_decode_latency + (1-latency_weight) * throughput_penalty + penalty_for_expected_handoffs.
- Add a prefill budget estimator that computes expected KV-cache growth and workspace pressure for the next N decode tokens and emits a prefill_budget score used by the selector to avoid kernels likely to trigger handoffs.
- Create telemetry hooks: per-request selected_kernel, handoff_events, prefill_budget, estimated_latency_ms, actual_decode_ms, and sequence_length_histogram.
- Run closed experimentation on a curated repro set (long-context QA, multi-turn chat, and small-batch burst traces). Compare p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU memory overhead, and cost-per-1000-tokens.

Acceptance criteria:
- p99 latency improvement >= 20% for latency-mode traces compared to baseline v3 selector while keeping throughput loss <= 10% and additional GPU memory <= 5% for the same workload mix.
- No increase in regression frequency for non-latency-mode traffic.
- Operational toggles for latency_weight and prefill_handoff_threshold exposed in runtime config and Redwood Console rollout UI.

Risks and mitigations:
- Selector complexity could oscillate under bursty traffic: add hysteresis and cooldown windows.
- Incorrect prefill_budget estimation could be conservative and hurt throughput: start with conservative default but surface telemetry to iterate.
- Interaction with quantized kernels: ensure selector can fall back to quant-aware compatibility list.

notes: Design trade-off: We prefer explicit request flags from product teams to avoid global SLO regressions. Console will allow route-level toggle.
If experiment shows large memory overheads, we'll explore a lightweight latency-only microkernel shim instead of full kernel biasing.
